question: Which company originally created the Android operating system before Google acquired it in 2005?
explanation: Android Inc. was founded in Palo Alto, California in 2003 by Andy Rubin, Rich Miner, Nick Sears, and Chris White before Google bought it.
funFact: Andy Rubin originally developed Android as an OS for digital cameras, not smartphones!

question: What does the 'GPT' in ChatGPT stand for?
explanation: GPT stands for Generative Pre-trained Transformer, based on the Transformer architecture introduced by Google researchers in 2017.
funFact: The breakthrough 'Attention Is All You Need' paper revolutionized modern AI in just 11 pages!

question: What was the very first video ever uploaded to YouTube in April 2005?
explanation: 'Me at the zoo' was uploaded by YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim at the San Diego Zoo on April 23, 2005.
funFact: The video is only 19 seconds long and shows elephants in the background!

question: Which programming language was originally called 'Oak' before being renamed?
explanation: James Gosling named Java 'Oak' after an oak tree outside his office window at Sun Microsystems.
funFact: It was renamed to Java after the popular Indonesian coffee consumed by the development team!

question: In what year did the legendary chess AI 'Deep Blue' defeat World Champion Garry Kasparov?
explanation: IBM's Deep Blue defeated Garry Kasparov in a 6-game match in May 1997, marking a milestone in artificial intelligence history.
funFact: Kasparov initially accused IBM of cheating by having a human grandmaster secretly intervene!

question: What is the highest-grossing film of all time globally (unadjusted for inflation)?
explanation: James Cameron's 2009 sci-fi epic Avatar has grossed over $2.92 Billion worldwide across multiple re-releases.
funFact: James Cameron waited over 10 years to film Avatar until 3D camera technology caught up with his vision!

question: Which superhero movie won Heath Ledger a posthumous Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor?
explanation: Heath Ledger won the Oscar for his iconic performance as the Joker in Christopher Nolan's 2008 masterpiece The Dark Knight.
funFact: Heath Ledger spent a month locked alone in a London hotel room developing the Joker's eerie voice, mannerisms, and diary!

question: In the Netflix smash-hit 'Stranger Things', what is the name of the parallel dark dimension?
explanation: The dark alternate reflection of Hawkins, Indiana is known throughout the series as The Upside Down.
funFact: The Duffer Brothers initially pitched the show under the working title 'Montauk'!

question: What is the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing—not even light—can escape?
explanation: The Event Horizon is the threshold where gravitational pull becomes infinite and escape velocity exceeds the speed of light.
funFact: If you fell into a stellar-mass black hole, gravitational stretching would turn you into cosmic spaghetti ('Spaghettification')!

question: How long does light from the Sun take to travel across space and reach Earth?
explanation: Traveling at 300,000 km/s across 149.6 Million km, sunlight takes roughly 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach our eyes.
funFact: If the Sun vanished right this second, Earth would stay lit and in orbit for another 8 minutes and 20 seconds!

question: Which ancient Wonder of the World is the only one that still largely stands intact today?
explanation: Built circa 2560 BC for Pharaoh Khufu, the Great Pyramid of Giza is the oldest and only surviving Wonder of the Ancient World.
funFact: The Great Pyramid was the tallest man-made structure on Earth for over 3,800 years!

question: Which Roman Emperor famously made his beloved horse Incitatus a Roman senator (or promised to)?
explanation: Emperor Caligula pampered his horse with an ivory stable, purple blankets, and threatened to appoint him consul to mock the Senate.
funFact: Caligula's real name was Gaius Julius Caesar Augustus Germanicus; 'Caligula' means 'Little Boot'!

question: What is the best-selling video game of all time with over 300 million copies sold?
explanation: Mojang's sandbox phenomenon Minecraft has sold over 300 Million units across all platforms worldwide.
funFact: Markus 'Notch' Persson created the first playable version of Minecraft in just a single weekend in May 2009!

question: In the anime 'Dragon Ball Z', what iconic power level number does Vegeta famously scream over his scouter?
explanation: In the famous English dub, Vegeta crushes his scouter and yells 'It's over 9,000!' when measuring Goku's raw power.
funFact: In the original Japanese manga and anime, Vegeta actually said 'Over 8,000!' (Hassen) — the English voice actors altered it for lip sync!

question: What was the very first item ever sold on Amazon in 1995?
explanation: Jeff Bezos founded Amazon as an online bookstore; the first book sold was Douglas Hofstadter's 'Fluid Concepts and Creative Analogies'.
funFact: Amazon was originally called 'Cadabra' (as in Abracadabra), but Bezos changed it after a lawyer misheard it as 'Cadaver'!

question: How many hearts does an octopus possess?
explanation: Octopuses have 3 hearts: two pump blue copper-rich blood to the gills, while the central systemic heart pumps blood through the rest of the body.
funFact: When an octopus swims, its main systemic heart actually stops beating, which is why they prefer crawling on the seafloor!

question: Which food item never spoils and has been found edible inside 3,000-year-old ancient Egyptian tombs?
explanation: Pure honey has low moisture, high acidity, and hydrogen peroxide produced by bees, making it completely impossible for bacteria to grow.
funFact: Archaeologists exploring Egyptian pyramids have tasted 3,000-year-old honey and confirmed it was still delicious!
